questions.question:

The average and rms values of the current, respectively, are.

The Correct Answer is Option "1".

 

__Concept:__

To find the average and RMS (root mean square) values of the given AC current, we'll use the following formulas,

begin{align*} Iₐvg &= (1)/(T) int₀^T i(t) dt \ end{align*} 

begin{align*} Iᵣₘₛ &= sqrt{(1)/(T) int₀^T [i(t)]² dt} end{align*} 

The integral of sin(wt) over one complete cycle is zero, resulting in Iₐvg=0 for a DC signal, the average value is equal to the amplitude of the signal.

__Calculation:__

​​i = 10 + 10 sin 314t

**therefore Iₐvg =10+0=10A**

For a sinusoidal signal, : RMS=(A)/(sqrt2)=(10)/(sqrt2)=7.07

therefore Iᵣₘₛ =sqrt{10²+{7.07}²}=12.24 ~A.

questions.question: The maximum value of power factor is:
questions.solution:
__Power Factor:__

 
• The overall power factor is defined as the cosine of the angle between the voltage and current. 
 
• In AC circuits, the power factor is also defined as the ratio of the real power flowing to the load to the apparent power in the circuit. Hence power factor can also be defined as the ratio of watts to volt-amperes.
 
• It is also defined as the ratio of resistance to the impedance of the circuit.
 
• The capacitor is used for power factor improvement.

 

Power Triangle:

The power factor is easily analyzed by the power triangle of the AC circuit.

If each side of the current triangle is multiplied by voltage V, then we get the power triangle as shown.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4faaf1bb5a3364ebf81ca0ff8855901388bf2512699a7564c6b2bc97435fa2b9.png] 

Power factor = cos ϕ

OA = VI cos φ and represents the active power in watts or kW

AB = VI sin φ and represents the reactive power in VAR or kVAR

OB = VI and represents the apparent power in VA or kVA

OB2 = OA2 + AB2

(kVA)2 = (kW)2 + (kVAR)2

cosϕ = frac{{OA}}{{OB}} = frac{{kW}}{{kVA}} .... (1)

From equation (1),

The maximum value of the power factor will be achieved when,

kW = kVA (According to Power triangle, kW cannot be more than kVA)

In this case,

cos φ = cos φM = 1

Hence, The maximum value of the power factor is 1.

An alternating current is given by the expression i(t) = 60 sin 314t. Calculate the frequency.
questions.solution:
__Concept:__

Considered a sinusoidal Alternating wave of voltage and current

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/14b9095e5ac271b4ac05b5d3c9e821c50946ae8153de87bb44a0df5493d93594.png] 

From the waveform:

 v = {V_m}sin ( {omega t} ) 

And,

i = {I_m}sin ( {omega t + ϕ } )

Where Vm and Im are the maximum value of instantaneous voltage and current respectively.

v, i is the instantaneous value of voltage and current at any instant t.

ω is the angular frequency in radian/second.

And, ω = 2πf 

f is the frequency in Hz

ϕ is the phase difference between voltage and current

From the above three equations instantaneous value of voltage and current can be written as: is

v = {V_m}sin ( {2pi ft} ) 

And,

i = {I_m}sin ( {2pi ft + ϕ } ) 

__Calculation:__

Sinusoidal wave is given as,

i(t) = 60 sin 314t

Comparing to the given equation

omega t = 2pi ft = 314t 

 f=(314)/(2pi)

∴ f = 50 Hz

We know that,

T = (1)/(f) = frac{{1 }}{{50}} = 0.02 sec = 20 ms

questions.question: RMS value is defined based on which of the following?
questions.solution:
**__Concept__**

__RMS (Root mean square) value__:

 
• RMS value is based on the heating effect of waveforms.
 
• The value at which the heat dissipated in the AC circuit is the same as the heat dissipated in the DC circuit is called the RMS value provided, both the AC and DC circuits have equal value of resistance and are operated at the same time.

 

The average or mean value of alternating current is the value of steady current which sends the same amount of charge through the circuit in a certain interval of time as is sent by alternating current through the same circuit in the same interval of time

questions.question: The value of reactive power drawn by a pure resistor is __________.
questions.solution:
__Resistor:__

__
 
• A resistor limits the electrical current that flows through a circuit.
 
• Resistance is the restriction of current.
 
• The resistor dissipates the power into heat in Watts.
 
• The power taken by the reactance is called reactive power.

Formula:

Apparent power S is

begin{array}{l} S = P + jQ\ S = VIcos emptyset + jVIsin emptyset end{array}

True power P = VIcos emptyset Watts

Reactive power Q = VIsin emptyset Var

The resistor dissipates electrical power =I².R in watts into heat in the form of True power.

The reactive power due to resistor is 0. 

Important points:__

 
• An inductor stores the energy in the form of magnetic energy(Kinetic energy)
 
• A Capacitor stores the energy into electrical energy(potential energy).
